chapter: Big band, Chicago players, recordings and gospel
title: Monday night sessions and Gene Ammons's influence on tenor players
summary: Saunders says tenors such as Lucious Washington and Prince James show Jug's influence, which he takes as the answer to Chicago's style.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: Yeah, I remember when I first came to Chicago in the '60s, there were sessions every Monday night. Segal used to have sessions, and they'd present names --
Right, Johnny Griffin and Gene Ammons.

This is why the influence -- I have a tenor player with me now, Lucious Washington, and everybody that hears him for the first time,they hear the influence of Jug in him. Because so many of the guys -- there's another guy around here named Prince James, I don't know whether you know him.
And he has that Jug influence.

Right, right, yes, Jug. But, see, so I think that that kind of answers your question as to -- about Chicago's style, because if you have a style that come out of a town like that, you have so many guys who are influenced by him. And it just creates the thing for the whole city.
That's right. Yeah, well, the musician is going to be influenced, particularly in jazz.
